summary: Teams create a three to five minute news broadcast on the rise of student entrepreneurship, featuring live interviews, a weather segment, and a promo. The project must include a script/creative brief and is judged on both technical and presentation criteria. Teams also complete an on-site one-minute news segment at nationals using provided materials.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes for setup
No more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation
No more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
Finals: no more than four (4) hours to plan, produce, and export a one (1:00) minute news segment
submission_requirements: Submit the following in one combined PDF: Clickable URL to Broadcast, Script/Creative Brief, Works Cited, BPA Release Form(s), AI Usage and Documentation Form
Upload completed projects to a video/file sharing link (Vimeo, YouTube, Dropbox, etc.)
Projects must be viewable on Windows and Mac platforms
Set the access level of your project to one of BPA’s recommended settings
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for presentation (projection equipment and external displays not provided or permitted)
Film equipment (computer, software, camera, etc.) for NLC
competencies: Utilize industry-standard broadcast software, hardware, and workflows to plan, capture, and edit high-quality broadcast content, integrating nonlinear editing techniques and strategic use of B-roll to enhance storytelling and production value
Create and refine broadcast scripts and scripting techniques to craft compelling, concise, and audience-focused stories
Design and implement effective introductions, segways, titles, lower thirds, and visual effects to structure broadcast segments, maintain engagement, and reinforce branding

Collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary broadcast teams, apply copyright and licensing laws, and conduct professional interviews with strong on-air presence to ensure ethical, engaging, and compliant broadcast content

rubric.criterion: Team followed the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy.

Team submitted the correct information, in the correct format, as one (1) PDF file. 1. Clickable URL to Broadcast 2. Script/Creative Brief 3. Works Cited (formatted in accordance with the Style & Reference Manual ) 4. BPA Release Form(s) 5. AI Usage and Documentation Form
Broadcast News Production made effective use of time and was within the video time limit of 3 -5 minutes.

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 1 No AI Allowed
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the contestants within the time allotted
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
No materials may be left with the judges
Only the team captain should complete the submission
No presentation for the finals round at the National Leadership Conference. Scoring from the preliminary round will not be included in finals scoring. Video is judged on technical merit only.
Teams will have no more than four (4) hours to plan, produce, and export a news segment of one (1:00) minute in length.
Teams will each receive a flash drive containing graphics and B-roll, which must be included in the news package.

Teams will film their production on site. During this time, students may communicate with contestants of their team via telephone but may not communicate with others (including their advisor) concerning the production of their video. Team will be disqualified for violating this rule.
After filming is complete, teams will return to the contest room to edit and complete all production and post-production elements in their video.

The video must be one (1:00) minute in length, rendered and exported into a MOV, MP4, AVI, MKV or MPG format and submitted using the provided flash drive. If video is not in the appropriate format, it may not be judged.
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring.
PRESENTATION WILL BE STOPPED AT TEN (10) MINUTES
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged team event.
A team will consist of 2 -4 contestants.
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked.
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Each state is allowed three (3) entries.
